A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GateSkip study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, allowing additions and deletions to be distinguished from relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark evaluations, component ablations, latency measurements, translation results, and gate-activation analyses, including detailed appendix results.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical evaluations and reports revised benchmark estimates, additional training ablations, and new gate-activation and timing analyses.

M1.justification: The default residual-gating method and Algorithms 1–3 remain unchanged. Section 4.4 adds experimental training variants using L1 and layer-wise Bernoulli-KL regularization, plus gate-only training on a frozen, previously fine-tuned backbone. These extend the tested training procedures without replacing the default method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain CSQA/GSM8K reasoning data, FineWeb, the same log-likelihood benchmarks, MMLU/PIQA generative evaluations, LAMBADA, and WMT16 English–Romanian translation. The new ablations and token-category analysis introduce no identified additional dataset or distinct task. Removing detailed appendix results does not remove the corresponding coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 add a separately labeled MoD comparator alongside the retained MoD (router-tuned). Table 2 also adds both FREE variants, LayerSkip, and SkipLayer to the task-level comparison at 15% savings; these methods already appeared in v1's aggregate Table 1. This is a bounded expansion of the comparison set.

E3.justification: V3 introduces controlled loss substitutions and a protocol that freezes an already fine-tuned backbone before training gates. Section 4.6 also changes the stated timing environment from explicitly not using vLLM to an optimized vLLM environment. Table 10 remains numerically identical, so this documents a setting revision without establishing a timing rerun. Existing benchmark splits, metrics, and stated budget sweeps remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 5 and Section 4.4 add substantive tests of regularizer choice and the necessity of backbone adaptation. Appendix C.3 adds corpus-level comparisons of gate activations across token categories and layers. Existing aggregate design ablations remain, but their detailed per-task curves and tables in v1's Appendices J–K are removed. Together these substantially revise the diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: V1 explicitly reports one seed per configuration with uncertainty estimated using 100,000 bootstrap resamples. V3 explicitly reports five seeds, identifies seeds 1–5, and presents means and standard deviations in Tables 1–2. This changes the source of uncertainty estimates, rather than merely adding error bars. V1's detailed bootstrap-uncertainty appendix is removed, while many retained tables still lack uncertainty values.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 are extensively revised under the new repeated-run reporting. For example, Table 1's GateSkip generative accuracy at 15% savings changes from 23.2 to 22.14±1.36, and router-tuned MoD's full-compute generative result changes from 20.1 to 0.00±0.00. These are revised estimates, not evidence of a method-level performance change. New ablation and diagnostic results are added, and detailed results across compute budgets are removed with v1's Appendices J–K. Tables 3–4 and 6–12 retain their numerical values.

T1.justification: Section 4.4 newly defines a layer-wise KL regularizer comparing Bernoulli distributions parameterized by mean gate activation and the target training budget. The original residual-gating, sparsity-loss, and quantile equations remain unchanged. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about residual gating, stable fine-tuning, reasoning accuracy under compute savings, instruction-model gains, and compatibility with other efficiency techniques. The added experiments do not redefine the stated principal contributions.

C2.justification: V3 adds the interpretation that backbone adaptation exposes relevance cues needed by gates. Appendix C.3 proposes semantic-processing and knowledge-checking explanations for attention and MLP activation patterns. The single-seed limitation is removed, and the expectation of future gains from optimized inference is replaced by a description of optimized execution. The broader interpretations and applicability boundaries remain largely intact.

D1.justification: V3 removes v1's named GitHub access link while retaining the anonymous repository, checkpoint availability statement, and setup instructions. The timing implementation is now described as using vLLM, without corresponding version or configuration details. Existing optimizer settings, training templates, hardware descriptions, and software-version listings are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: The bibliography and substantive related-work discussion are unchanged. GateSkip retains the same positioning relative to hard routing, early exiting, pruning, and quantization. The additional MoD comparison does not come with revised research-positioning claims.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes comprise localized experimental and analytical paragraphs, revised statistical and timing descriptions, updated appendix references, and publication-header and affiliation edits. The appendix organization changes through added subsections and removal of the plot/raw-result sections, without a broad rewrite of the narrative.

P2.justification: V3 removes v1's Figures 6–24 and Tables 15–50, adds the token-category heatmap and FLOPs/time plot, and expands Tables 1–2 and 5. Table captions move above tables, and Tables 1–2 use substantially smaller type to accommodate additional rows and uncertainty values. Existing gate heatmaps and distribution figures are retained with renumbering.

improvement.justification: Five-seed comparisons and new regularizer/backbone controls strengthen evidence beyond v1's single-seed study. However, v3 removes detailed results across budgets and leaves revised evidence unreconciled with the narrative: Section 4.3 still quotes 36.7/9.7 for GateSkip where Table 2 now reports 35.25/9.03. It also attributes unchanged Table 10 timings to vLLM after v1 explicitly excluded that environment. The statistical gains coexist with reduced transparency and uncertainty about which conditions support the reported results, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
